extracted.intended_audience: audience members attending TheatreSports shows; improv performers, moderators, and event staff
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and guidance for running and judging a team-based TheatreSports improv competition (how audience voting works, moderator duties, scum box usage, and tournament structure) as presented by a producing theatre.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience voting (1–5 applause scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Audience voting occurs at the end of each scene. The moderator will ask the audience to rank the scene on a scale of one to five using their applause—with five as the highest possible score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For example, if an audience member believes a scene deserves a one, they would cheer when the referee announces, “ONE!” If they believe a scene deserves a two, they would cheer when the referee announces, “TWO!”, etc. The number with the loudest amount of applause is the score for that round.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderator / judges responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Every performance is hosted by a moderator (or panel of judges, in the tournament’s case) that oversees the competition, tallies audience votes, and dispenses the scum box whenever needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moderators may act solo or as a panel (especially during tournaments); they tally audience applause votes and make discretionary decisions such as when to deploy the scum box. (The page notes moderators sometimes dress up as judges.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Scum box usage and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The scum box is a wonderful invention designed to keep improvisers—and patrons, if the situation calls for it—from getting too rowdy during a performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational details: It is a cardboard box worn on the head at the discretion of the moderator. If someone else becomes crazier, the scum box transfers to them. It doesn’t come out every performance, but it is always at the ready. (Implied criterion: moderator discretion and transferability are permitted behaviors.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of audience suggestions to fuel scenes
rubrics_metrics.description: TheatreSports is a fast-paced improv competition that features the best improvisers in the city and uses your suggestions to fuel the show.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied requirement for performers: scenes should be based on or incorporate audience suggestions provided during the performance, supporting spontaneity and audience engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition outcome (winner determination)
rubrics_metrics.description: They’re battling for your laughs — there WILL be a winner!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied scoring policy: audience applause-based scores per scene are tallied by the moderator/judges to produce a winner for the competition or match.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tournament structure and continuity
rubrics_metrics.description: In January, Dad’s Garage holds a three-week long tournament of TheatreSports every Friday and Saturday.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational guidance: attendees are encouraged to choose a favorite team and cheer them on week after week to victory; tournament performances may use a panel of judges and follow the same audience-voting procedures across multiple weeks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance runtime
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical guideline for planning and expectations: shows are approximately one hour long; this frames the number of scenes and the pacing for voting and moderator interventions.
